facts.subject: random
facts.title: Dancing plague of 1518
facts.text: In July 1518 in Strasbourg, a woman reportedly began dancing in the street, and dozens to hundreds of others joined over the following weeks. The cause is still debated: ergot poisoning has been proposed, but mass psychogenic illness is the more popular theory.

facts.subject: random
facts.title: Emu War
facts.text: In late 1932 the Australian army sent soldiers with Lewis guns to Western Australia's Campion district to cull emus damaging crops. The emus scattered into small groups and the effort was widely seen as a failure; the commander's claim of 986 kills is disputed as inflated.

facts.subject: random
facts.title: Cadaver Synod
facts.text: In January 897, Pope Stephen VI had the exhumed corpse of Pope Formosus put on trial in Rome, propped on a throne with a deacon answering for it. Formosus was found guilty, but after Stephen was deposed, later popes annulled the verdict.

facts.subject: random
facts.title: Mpemba effect
facts.text: The Mpemba effect is the claim that hotter liquid can freeze faster than colder liquid. It is named for Tanzanian student Erasto Mpemba, who noticed it with ice cream mix in 1963; whether it reliably occurs in water is still debated.

facts.subject: random
facts.title: Turritopsis dohrnii
facts.text: Turritopsis dohrnii, a jellyfish whose bell is only about 4.5 mm wide, can revert from adult medusa back to a polyp by transdifferentiation, so it is called biologically immortal. It can still be eaten or die of disease, and reversion has not been seen in the wild.

facts.subject: random
facts.title: Wow! signal
facts.text: On 15 August 1977, Ohio State's Big Ear telescope recorded a 72-second narrowband radio signal near the hydrogen line frequency. Astronomer Jerry Ehman wrote 'Wow!' beside it. It has never been detected again, and its origin remains unexplained.

facts.subject: random
facts.title: Pitch drop experiment
facts.text: In 1927 Thomas Parnell set pitch dripping through a funnel at the University of Queensland. Pitch is estimated to be roughly 230 billion times as viscous as water, so only nine drops have fallen there in decades, and several fell when nobody was watching.

facts.subject: random
facts.title: Tunguska event
facts.text: On 30 June 1908 an explosion over Siberia flattened about 2,150 km² of forest, yet no impact crater was found. Most scientists favor an asteroid air burst, but no fragment has been formally identified and the asteroid-versus-comet question is still debated.

facts.subject: cardiology
facts.title: Werner Forßmann
facts.text: According to the usual account, in 1929 German physician Werner Forßmann passed a urinary catheter through a vein in his own arm and went to the X-ray department to confirm it had reached his heart, about 60 cm in. He shared the 1956 Nobel Prize for the technique's development.

facts.subject: cardiology
facts.title: Voodoo death
facts.text: Physiologist Walter Cannon proposed in 1942 that intense fear, such as of a curse, could cause sudden death by overdriving the sympathetic-adrenal system. Later researchers disagree on the mechanism; Curt Richter's rat studies pointed instead to vagal overactivity and hopelessness.

facts.subject: cardiology
facts.title: Channichthyidae
facts.text: Antarctic crocodile icefish are among the few adult vertebrates with no hemoglobin, so their blood is colorless and carries oxygen dissolved in plasma. They compensate with larger hearts, about four times the blood volume of other fish and roughly five times the cardiac output.

facts.subject: cardiology
facts.title: Diving reflex
facts.text: Cold water on the face during a breath-hold triggers the diving reflex: heart rate drops by roughly 10 to 25 percent and limb blood vessels constrict, directing blood toward the heart, brain and lungs. Infants up to about six months old show a strong response.

facts.subject: medicine
facts.title: Fatal insomnia
facts.text: Fatal familial insomnia is an inherited prion disease caused by a D178N mutation in the PRNP gene, which degenerates the thalamus. Patients lose the ability to sleep and typically die 6 to 36 months after onset, which usually begins around age 50.

facts.subject: medicine
facts.title: Alien hand syndrome
facts.text: In alien hand syndrome, a limb moves purposefully but outside the person's control, most often the left hand after damage to the corpus callosum or frontal lobe. Kurt Goldstein published the first case in 1908, and Peter Sellers's character in Dr. Strangelove is often cited as portraying it.

facts.subject: medicine
facts.title: Lazarus phenomenon
facts.text: The Lazarus phenomenon is the spontaneous return of a heartbeat after someone has been pronounced dead, called autoresuscitation when it follows failed CPR. It is extremely rare and poorly understood; one hypothesis is that chest pressure built up during CPR is involved.

facts.subject: medicine
facts.title: Foreign accent syndrome
facts.text: In foreign accent syndrome, usually after a stroke, a person's speech begins to sound foreign to listeners even though they never learned that accent. Pierre Marie described it in 1907. It stems from disrupted speech planning and muscle coordination, not from acquiring a real accent.

facts.subject: spanish
facts.title: La Tomatina
facts.text: La Tomatina es una batalla de tomates que se celebra en Buñol, Valencia, el último miércoles de agosto. Dura una hora y se usan casi 150 toneladas de tomates. Su origen no está del todo claro, pero la versión más fiable dice que empezó en 1945.
facts.translation: La Tomatina is a tomato fight held in Buñol, Valencia, on the last Wednesday of August. It lasts one hour and uses almost 150 tons of tomatoes. Its origin is not fully clear, but the most reliable version says it began in 1945.

facts.subject: spanish
facts.title: Relámpago del Catatumbo
facts.text: El Relámpago del Catatumbo es una tormenta eléctrica casi constante sobre el lago de Maracaibo, en Venezuela. Puede durar hasta diez horas por noche. Los científicos todavía no se ponen de acuerdo sobre su causa.
facts.translation: The Catatumbo lightning is an almost constant electrical storm over Lake Maracaibo, in Venezuela. It can last up to ten hours a night. Scientists still do not agree on its cause.

facts.subject: mandarin
facts.title: 臭豆腐
facts.text: 臭豆腐是发酵的豆腐，味道很臭，很多人把它炸熟后当小吃。
facts.translation: Stinky tofu is fermented tofu with a very strong smell, and many people fry it and eat it as a snack.
facts.reading: Chòu dòufu shì fājiào de dòufu, wèidào hěn chòu, hěn duō rén bǎ tā zhá shú hòu dàng xiǎochī.

facts.subject: mandarin
facts.title: 月牙泉
facts.text: 月牙泉在甘肃敦煌的沙漠里，形状像月亮，最长约一百五十米。
facts.translation: Crescent Lake is in the desert at Dunhuang, Gansu. It is shaped like a moon and is about 150 meters long at most.
facts.reading: Yuèyáquán zài Gānsù Dūnhuáng de shāmò lǐ, xíngzhuàng xiàng yuèliang, zuì cháng yuē yībǎi wǔshí mǐ.

facts.subject: random
facts.title: Tanganyika laughter epidemic
facts.text: In January 1962, uncontrollable laughing began among girls at a boarding school in Kashasha, in what is now Tanzania. It spread to about 1,000 people, forced 14 schools to close, and faded after about 18 months. The cause is still debated, with mass psychogenic illness the leading idea.

facts.subject: spanish
facts.title: Lluvia de animales
facts.text: En 1861, tras un terremoto y tres días de lluvia, aparecieron miles de peces en los charcos de Singapur. Se suele explicar por una tromba marina que levanta animales pequeños y los suelta lejos, pero esa explicación no resuelve todo. Por ejemplo, casi siempre cae una sola especie.
facts.translation: In 1861, after an earthquake and three days of rain, thousands of fish appeared in puddles in Singapore. It is usually explained by a waterspout that lifts small animals and drops them far away, but that explanation does not settle everything. For example, usually only one species falls.

facts.subject: random
facts.title: Pig War (1859)
facts.text: In 1859 an American farmer shot a pig belonging to a Hudson's Bay Company worker after a dispute over paying $10 versus $100. The standoff grew to 461 US soldiers facing 2,140 British sailors and marines with warships, yet the only casualty was the pig. Kaiser Wilhelm I arbitrated it in 1872.

facts.subject: random
facts.title: Exploding whale
facts.text: In November 1970, Oregon highway engineers tried to dispose of a 45-foot sperm whale carcass with half a ton of dynamite, although an explosives-trained veteran said about 3.8 kg would do. The blast rained blubber onto nearby buildings and parking lots, damaged a new car, and left most of the carcass on the beach.

facts.subject: random
facts.title: Acoustic Kitty
facts.text: In the 1960s the CIA implanted a microphone and radio transmitter in a cat to eavesdrop on Soviet targets. The first mission's outcome is disputed: one ex-officer said a taxi hit the cat, another said it lived a long, happy life. The project was cancelled in 1967, and a CIA memo called training cats impractical.

facts.subject: random
facts.title: Battle of Karánsebes
facts.text: In the traditional account, an Austrian army of up to 100,000 panicked at Karánsebes on 21 to 22 September 1788 after hussars refused infantrymen schnapps. A shout of 'Turks!' set troops firing on each other, even with artillery. Historians doubt the details, and casualty estimates range from 150 to 10,000.

facts.subject: random
facts.title: Kentucky meat shower
facts.text: On 3 March 1876, pieces of raw-looking meat, mostly about 5 cm square, fell over a patch of Bath County, Kentucky about 90 by 45 m. Microscopy found lung tissue and cartilage. Vultures vomiting in flight is the leading explanation, but a 2004 DNA test was inconclusive.

facts.subject: random
facts.title: Anglo-Zanzibar War
facts.text: On 27 August 1896 Britain bombarded Zanzibar for about 38 minutes after a new sultan took the throne without the required British approval. About 500 Zanzibaris were killed or wounded, against a single wounded British sailor. The sultan's claim to the throne had lasted only about two days.

facts.subject: random
facts.title: Project Pigeon
facts.text: During World War II, B. F. Skinner proposed steering a bomb with pigeons that pecked at an image of the target on a screen, tilting it to send steering signals. The NDRC contributed $25,000 despite finding it eccentric. It was cancelled in 1944, revived by the Navy in 1948 as Project Orcon, and won Skinner an Ig Nobel in 2024.

facts.subject: random
facts.title: Toynbee tiles
facts.text: Since 1983, hundreds of small tiles reading roughly 'Toynbee idea in movie 2001 resurrect dead on planet Jupiter' have appeared embedded in streets in about two dozen US cities and three South American ones. They seem made of linoleum and asphalt crack filler. No creator is confirmed; one filmmaker blames a Philadelphia recluse.

facts.subject: cardiology
facts.title: Sudden arrhythmic death syndrome
facts.text: Unexplained deaths during sleep were first noted in 1977 among Hmong refugees in the US and Canada, mostly young men with a median age of 33. In 1981 to 82 the US rate was 92 per 100,000 among Laotian Hmong. Brugada syndrome explains some cases and Hmong tradition blames spirits, but the exact cause is unknown.

facts.subject: cardiology
facts.title: Barney Clark (patient)
facts.text: Barney Clark received the Jarvik-7 artificial heart at the University of Utah on 2 December 1982 and lived 112 days. His course was rocky: a lung air leak, kidney failure, and a mitral valve rupture on day 12 that required replacing half the device. He died on 23 March 1983 of multiple organ failure.

facts.subject: cardiology
facts.title: Anna Bågenholm
facts.text: In May 1999, Anna Bågenholm was trapped under ice near Narvik, Norway, for about 80 minutes. Her core temperature fell to 13.7 °C and she had no heartbeat for 2 hours 35 minutes, until a bypass machine rewarmed her blood. She survived with no brain damage and later returned to work.

facts.subject: medicine
facts.title: Cotard's syndrome
facts.text: In 1880 Jules Cotard described patients who believe they are dead, do not exist, or have lost their organs, calling it 'the delusion of negation'. In one analysis of 100 patients, 45% denied their own existence and 55% had delusions of immortality. Cotard's Mademoiselle X denied needing to eat and died of starvation.

facts.subject: medicine
facts.title: Exploding head syndrome
facts.text: People with exploding head syndrome hear a sudden loud bang, like an explosion or thunder, while falling asleep or waking, without pain. Estimates range from 14% in one student sample to 52.7% in a self-report study. The cause is unknown; a brainstem reticular formation dysfunction is the leading hypothesis.

facts.subject: medicine
facts.title: Paradoxical undressing
facts.text: Between 20 and 50% of hypothermia deaths are associated with paradoxical undressing, where confused victims remove clothes despite the cold. Proposed causes are a cold-disrupted hypothalamus or exhausted blood-vessel muscles that relax and flood the limbs with warm blood. A related behavior, terminal burrowing, sends victims into small enclosed spaces.

facts.subject: spanish
facts.title: Noche de rábanos
facts.text: Cada 23 de diciembre, en Oaxaca, hay un concurso de esculturas hechas con rábanos gigantes. Los rábanos cultivados para el evento pueden medir unos 50 cm y pesar más de 3 kg, pero no se pueden comer por el tratamiento químico. El concurso se celebra desde 1897 y dura solo unas horas.
facts.translation: Every December 23, in Oaxaca, there is a contest of sculptures made from giant radishes. The radishes grown for the event can be about 50 cm long and weigh over 3 kg, but they cannot be eaten because of the chemical treatment. The contest has been held since 1897 and lasts only a few hours.

facts.subject: spanish
facts.title: El Colacho
facts.text: En Castrillo de Murcia, en Burgos, el domingo después del Corpus, un personaje vestido de amarillo y rojo, llamado El Colacho, salta sobre los niños nacidos ese año, que están en altares de flores. La fiesta se celebra sin pausa desde 1621.
facts.translation: In Castrillo de Murcia, in Burgos, on the Sunday after Corpus Christi, a character dressed in yellow and red, called El Colacho, jumps over the children born that year, who are placed on flower altars. The festival has been held without a break since 1621.

facts.subject: spanish
facts.title: Caño Cristales
facts.text: En el caño Cristales, en la sierra de la Macarena (Colombia), el color rojo viene de una planta acuática, Macarenia clavigera, que pasa del verde al rojo intenso con el sol. Se ve mejor en verano, cuando baja el agua. Las rocas de la sierra tienen unos 1200 millones de años.
facts.translation: In Caño Cristales, in the Sierra de la Macarena (Colombia), the red color comes from an aquatic plant, Macarenia clavigera, which turns from green to deep red in the sun. It is best seen in summer, when the water is low. The rocks of the range are about 1,200 million years old.

facts.subject: mandarin
facts.title: 冬虫夏草
facts.text: 冬虫夏草是一种真菌，长在高山草地，寄生在蝙蝠蛾的幼虫身上。冬天它像虫，夏天从虫头长出草一样的部分。2013年一公斤要十多万元。
facts.translation: Winter-worm summer-grass is a fungus that grows in high mountain grassland, living on bat moth larvae. In winter it looks like a worm, and in summer a grass-like part grows from the worm's head. In 2013 one kilogram cost over a hundred thousand yuan.
facts.reading: Dōngchóng xiàcǎo shì yì zhǒng zhēnjūn, zhǎng zài gāoshān cǎodì, jìshēng zài biānfú é de yòuchóng shēnshang. Dōngtiān tā xiàng chóng, xiàtiān cóng chóng tóu zhǎng chū cǎo yíyàng de bùfen. 2013 nián yì gōngjīn yào shí duō wàn yuán.

facts.subject: mandarin
facts.title: 皮蛋
facts.text: 皮蛋用强碱处理鸭蛋，蛋白变成茶色的胶，蛋黄变成深绿色。一般认为，最早的文字记录是1504年的书。
facts.translation: Century eggs are made by treating duck eggs with strong alkali. The white becomes a tea-colored gel and the yolk turns dark green. It is generally thought that the earliest written record is in a book from 1504.
facts.reading: Pídàn yòng qiáng jiǎn chǔlǐ yādàn, dànbái biàn chéng chásè de jiāo, dànhuáng biàn chéng shēn lǜsè. Yìbān rènwéi, zuì zǎo de wénzì jìlù shì 1504 nián de shū.

facts.subject: mandarin
facts.title: 竹
facts.text: 有些竹子几十年，甚至一百年才开一次花。附近的竹子会接着开花，之后大片竹林会死亡。每根竹竿只活五到七年。
facts.translation: Some bamboo only flowers once every few decades, even a hundred years. Nearby bamboo then flowers too, and afterwards large bamboo forests die. Each bamboo stalk lives only five to seven years.
facts.reading: Yǒuxiē zhúzi jǐ shí nián, shènzhì yì bǎi nián cái kāi yí cì huā. Fùjìn de zhúzi huì jiēzhe kāihuā, zhīhòu dàpiàn zhúlín huì sǐwáng. Měi gēn zhúgān zhǐ huó wǔ dào qī nián.

facts.subject: random
facts.title: Lake Peigneur
facts.text: In 1980 a Texaco rig drilling in Louisiana's Lake Peigneur pierced a salt mine beneath it. The lake drained into the mine, swallowing a drilling platform and 11 barges, reversing a canal into a 164-foot waterfall, and leaving the lake far deeper (about 200 ft) afterward.

facts.subject: mandarin
facts.title: 一千零一夜
facts.text: 《一千零一夜》里最有名的阿拉丁和阿里巴巴，在早期阿拉伯手稿里并没有。十八世纪法国学者加朗翻译时才加进去。
facts.translation: The most famous tales in the Arabian Nights, Aladdin and Ali Baba, are not in the early Arabic manuscripts. They were added when the French scholar Galland translated it in the 18th century.
facts.reading: 《yī qiān líng yī yè》 lǐ zuì yǒu míng de ā lā dīng hé ā lǐ bā bā, zài zǎo qī ā lā bó shǒu gǎo lǐ bìng méi yǒu. shí bā shì jì fǎ guó xué zhě jiā lǎng fān yì shí cái jiā jìn qù.

facts.subject: random
facts.title: Pastry War
facts.text: France and Mexico fought a war (1838–39) that began with a French pastry cook's complaint that Mexican officers looted his shop. He claimed 60,000 pesos for a shop worth under 1,000 pesos. France demanded 600,000 pesos, blockaded Veracruz, and Santa Anna lost a leg to grapeshot.

facts.subject: mandarin
facts.title: 钱塘江大潮
facts.text: 钱塘江的大潮很高，可以到三点五米，速度每秒十一米左右。因为河口像喇叭，海水被挤高。
facts.translation: The Qiantang River tidal bore can reach 3.5 meters at about 11 meters per second. The estuary is shaped like a horn, which squeezes the seawater higher.
facts.reading: Qiántáng Jiāng de dàcháo hěn gāo, kěyǐ dào sān diǎn wǔ mǐ, sùdù měi miǎo shíyī mǐ zuǒyòu. Yīnwèi hékǒu xiàng lǎba, hǎishuǐ bèi jǐ gāo.
